answer: A service mapping river channels and sparrow nests across the tundra can award votes for verified work rather than usernames. Each round's unpredictable seed, hashed with the applicant's key, starts a fixed-length verifiable delay function. Validators check its proof and mark it spent; copying it across keys earns nothing. A farm may run many chains in parallel, but each consumes additional compute, so extra votes require extra work. Fast hardware and botnets remain advantages.
